findings.evidence: template/scripts/finish_task.py:1047-1049 calls sync_queue_merged_task, which has its own local_status, SystemExit wrapping and sync_merged_task. The pre-existing block at lines 1058-1082 repeats the same sequence. The test change `side_effect=[waiting, waiting] if early else [None, None, waiting]` shows the double read. The helper could return the queued state so the later block could reuse it, or the later block could call the helper.
findings.summary: The merged-queue observation and sync is now implemented twice in finish_task.main. For a merged managed candidate, local_status and sync_merged_task each run twice (the second time after the fast-forward), which costs extra GitHub reads. The two copies can also drift apart.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/finish_task.py:128-133 (`except Exception ... raise SystemExit`) runs ahead of `run_finish_preflight` at line 1050. publication_queue.local_status (publication_queue.py:1665-1682) raises QueueError for an oversized or ambiguous PR inventory. The design.md Risks section lists only the extra read.
findings.summary: Every coordinator-managed candidate finish now makes a publication-queue observation before the handoff preflight. Any exception from local_status (a gh outage, a queue inventory error such as multiple admitted PRs on the branch, or the 100-entry page limit) becomes a SystemExit before the handoff. Previously only the later post-handoff path observed the queue. This is consistent with the fail-explicitly rule, but it widens the failure surface of the first submission. The design records only 'one extra PR read' as a risk.
